name: Histiocytic and Dendritic Cell Tumor

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues

criteria.description: Presence of large, pleomorphic histiocytic or dendritic cells with abundant cytoplasm and irregular nuclei on histopathology
Immunohistochemical positivity for histiocytic markers (CD68, CD163) and dendritic cell markers (CD1a, S100) with absence of lineage-specific markers for lymphoid or myeloid cells
Exclusion of other hematologic malignancies such as lymphoma, leukemia, and myeloid sarcoma by morphology and immunophenotyping
Detection of clonal genetic abnormalities such as BRAF V600E mutation or other MAPK pathway mutations (supportive)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathologic confirmation of characteristic morphology plus immunophenotypic evidence of histiocytic/dendritic lineage and exclusion of other hematologic malignancies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular studies may aid diagnosis but are not mandatory.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Localized tumorous mass of histiocytic or dendritic origin
pathognomonic.notes: Often presents as a solitary or multifocal mass lesion
searchTerms: mass from histiocyte or dendritic cells

pathognomonic.notes: Enlarged lymph nodes due to tumor infiltration
searchTerms: swollen lymph nodes with immune cell growth
lymph node enlargement with histiocyte increase

common.symptomName: Constitutional symptoms including unexplained weight loss
Bone pain due to skeletal involvement

common.notes: Enlargement of liver and spleen in disseminated disease

occasional.symptomName: Respiratory symptoms due to pulmonary infiltration
occasional.notes: Dyspnea or cough in lung involvement
searchTerms: lung symptoms due to tissue buildup

occasional.notes: Focal neurological signs if brain or spinal cord affected
searchTerms: neurological deficits from brain or spinal involvement
nerve problems due to CNS disease
weakness or sensory loss from CNS

occasional.symptomName: Abdominal pain from gastrointestinal tract infiltration
occasional.notes: May be related to mass effect or infiltration
searchTerms: abdominal discomfort due to GI involvement
heart issues caused by tumor spread

laboratory: Possible cytopenias in bone marrow involvement
imaging: CT or MRI showing mass lesions in lymph nodes, soft tissue, or organs
genetic: BRAF V600E mutation in subset of cases
Mutations in MAPK pathway genes (e.g., MAP2K1, KRAS)
other: Histopathology with large atypical histiocytic/dendritic cells
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD68, CD163, S100, CD1a depending on subtype

distinguishingFeatures: Peripheral blood and bone marrow involvement with blasts
Lineage-specific markers for myeloid or lymphoid cells
Often associated with acute myeloid leukemia

references: Swerdlow SH, Campo E, Harris NL, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues. IARC; 2017.
Feldman AL, Arber DA. Histiocytic and dendritic cell neoplasms: a review. Arch Pathol Lab Med. 2013;137(9):1241-1248.
